Forest County Potawatomi Community

Forest County Potawatomi Community is a distinct Potawatomi government whose public timeline connects wider Potawatomi history with a particular Wisconsin institutional history. It traces land purchase using treaty money in 1913 and identifies reorganization as the Forest County Potawatomi Community in 1937. Later entries describe a Tribal court, a community newspaper and the museum, showing several forms of institution building. Those local milestones should be distinguished from earlier events involving Potawatomi people more broadly. The Community's Cultural Preservation page provides a complementary route into public history. It describes a museum collection of photographs, recordings, manuscripts, treaties and language materials, alongside a tribally owned library focused on Native studies and Great Lakes communities. The library also maintains non-circulating research material, so a public catalog is not the same as unrestricted access to every collection item. The pictured Milwaukee hotel is part of the Community's casino enterprise, whose own page explicitly identifies the owner and operator. Together, these sources introduce history, cultural institutions and one economic institution, while leaving detailed chronology and outcomes for further study.

01

A local institutional timeline

The Community dates land purchase using treaty funds to 1913 and its reorganization to 1937. Its later chronology includes a Tribal court, newspaper and museum. These specific entries offer a route into Forest County history without merging every Potawatomi government.

Read the sources [1] Forest County Potawatomi Community

02

Museum and research library

The Cultural Preservation page describes photographs, recordings, manuscripts and language materials in the museum and a tribally owned public library. Its research library includes non-circulating material; collection access and individual provenance need separate review.

Read the sources [2] Forest County Potawatomi Community
